phases.title: Repository foundation and agent continuity
phases.goal: Establish truthful specifications and an executable continuation system before game implementation.
phases.exit_gate: Repository definitions, validation harness and a reproducible handoff exist; no game, graphics or hardware completion is implied.

tasks.title: Publish the product contract and engineering boundaries
deliverables: Explicit Duo-only, offline and no-puzzle scope
steps: Translate the owner's accepted concept into one launch-kit scope.
Separate Swift platform responsibilities from Three.js world responsibilities.
List verified platform facts separately from proposed performance targets.
Record unresolved naming and Duo-only distribution gates without declaring clearance.
Cross-link the boot path, subsystem specifications and release constraints.

acceptance.requirement: Product and architecture documents state the accepted scope, subsystem ownership and unresolved release constraints.
A new reader can locate the roadmap, ledger and handoff from root instructions without relying on chat.

tests: Check all required_reading paths and Markdown relative links.
Review forbidden monetization and puzzle features against the product specification.
risks: A large document volume can conceal missing operational instructions.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Install the task graph, evidence ledger and continuation validator
deliverables: Machine-readable dependency graph and mutable task ledger
steps: Define immutable task IDs, ordered phases and dependency edges.
Store mutable status, claims, blockers and evidence only in the ledger.
Generate human-readable phase pages, status and next-task projections.
Reject cycles, orphan tasks, false completion, absent evidence and invalid transitions.
Test active/stale claims, blocked dependencies and failed-CI priority.
Demonstrate a handoff and recovery without changing unrelated work.

acceptance.requirement: Repository validation and project-command tests pass for valid state and reject the documented invalid fixtures.
Repeated selection on identical state identifies the same next eligible task and explains blockers.

tests: Run the project validator and Node project test suite.
Mutate isolated fixture state to demonstrate failed dependencies cannot become done.
risks: Hand-edited generated dashboards can drift from the ledger.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Install diagnostic Swift and Three.js scaffolds with CI definitions
deliverables: Pinned web diagnostic build and offline native asset bundle
Unsigned simulator and repository-quality workflow definitions
steps: Pin dependency versions and commit the reproducible lockfile.
Create a plainly labelled engineering scene with no finished-game claim.
Connect native and web bootstrap diagnostics using the versioned envelope.
Add explicit toolchain and Duo simulator inventory assertions.
Upload logs and diagnostic artifacts on failures as well as success.
Keep signing and store publication outside ordinary push workflows.

acceptance.requirement: Web type checks, unit checks and bundled asset generation succeed with locked dependencies.
Native project and workflow files are installed with explicit SDK checks; unexecuted native checks are clearly disclosed.

tests: Run the web build and inspect the generated local bundle for remote-script dependencies.
Parse workflow YAML and verify every referenced tool/script path exists.
risks: Installing a workflow does not prove it ran or that the application is ready.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Verify and publish the initial repository handoff
steps: Run every available setup check and preserve actual output summaries.
Record any checks unavailable in the current environment rather than guessing outcomes.
Associate evidence with the tested implementation commit and source digests.
Publish the setup changes and confirm the intended remote main head.
Regenerate status and identify the first uncompleted platform task.
Record next actions, current CI state and owner-only release blockers.

acceptance.requirement: The setup evidence records actual commands/results and distinguishes local, browser, simulator and device validation.
Remote setup and a durable handoff are published; only satisfied setup tasks are marked done.

tests: Run project validation after the evidence/state update.
Verify remote main contains the reported files and handoff.
risks: A local-only handoff does not help the next agent.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

phases.title: Platform truth and packaged-runtime spikes
phases.goal: Prove the documented Duo SDK and the actual packaged WebView loading path before expanding the product.
phases.exit_gate: SDK/runtime assumptions have concrete evidence; unresolved commercial exclusivity remains a separately tracked release blocker.

tasks.title: Compile public Duo capabilities and inventory the CI device
deliverables: Captured Xcode, SDK and Duo simulator inventory
steps: Recheck official Apple API documentation and record retrieval dates.
Compile the minimal hinge observer using the selected supported SDK.
Enumerate real available simulator runtimes and dynamically select a Duo UDID.
Exercise launch and rotation without hardcoded screen dimensions.
Capture nil-hinge and geometry observations separately from physical-device evidence.
Document any unavailable CLI posture controls as gaps, not invented flags.

acceptance.requirement: A recorded Xcode build compiles the public hinge adapter and identifies the selected SDK and actual Duo simulator.
The evidence distinguishes supported API signatures from unverified physical-device and store assumptions.

tests: Run the unsigned native build on the documented runner.
Confirm a missing Duo runtime produces an explicit failure, not a generic-iPhone fallback.
risks: Runner image contents can change despite a stable label.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Prove bundled asset loading inside the actual WKWebView origin
deliverables: Minimal GLB, texture, audio and decoder fixtures
steps: Create original minimal fixture assets with recorded hashes.
Load the classic script bundle and create WebGL2 inside the packaged host.
Load a GLB and texture through the production origin, not the desktop preview server.
Probe KTX2/WASM and worker paths under the intended content security policy.
Exercise offline launch, cache clearing and repeat loading.
Record the selected transport approach and unresolved origin limitations in an ADR.

acceptance.requirement: Bundled code and fixture GLB/texture content render in the packaged native app with networking disabled.
Decoder, worker and audio probes report observed success or explicit blockers; unsupported loaders are not silently enabled.

tests: Inspect native/WebContent logs for origin, MIME, decoder and CSP errors.
Repeat after deleting app data and disabling network access.
risks: Browser HTTP success does not establish custom-scheme WKWebView compatibility.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Verify the custom-origin security boundary
steps: Define allowed host, scheme, resource root and MIME mappings.
Reject dot segments, encoded traversal, unexpected hosts and unsupported methods.
Cancel outstanding scheme tasks without calling stopped callbacks.
Block remote navigation and arbitrary file access.
Fuzz malformed bridge and resource requests within bounded limits.
Document evidence that no private WebKit security overrides are used.

acceptance.requirement: Traversal, unsupported origins, unknown resources and oversized messages fail safely without leaking files.
Cancellation and repeated process teardown complete without crashes or callbacks into invalid tasks.

tests: Run Swift resource-handler tests and packaged negative tests.
Inspect shipped native configuration for private KVC or unrestricted navigation.
risks: A permissive development host can accidentally become the production boundary.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Resolve approved Duo-only commercial distribution
deliverables: Release-blocker resolution or explicit stop decision
steps: Inspect Apple's current capability and distribution documentation.
Determine whether a supported capability or distribution route actually excludes non-Duo purchases.
Do not treat TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY or an in-app error screen as exclusivity.
Record official support guidance where public documentation is insufficient.
Present any unavoidable scope tradeoff to the owner.
Keep release blocked until the owner approves a documented route; do not broaden device scope automatically.

acceptance.requirement: A documented Apple-supported route satisfies the owner's exclusive-device requirement, or the owner explicitly approves a revised policy.
The approved policy is reflected in release gates and cannot be bypassed by an undocumented capability key.

tests: Review supported-device eligibility through the approved distribution workflow.
Verify unrelated engine tasks remain selectable while this gate is blocked.
risks: This task can block release without blocking independent development.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Measure a representative packaged rendering spike
deliverables: Initial device baseline and benchmark conditions
steps: Create an original neutral scene approximating intended material and instance counts.
Record scene seed, render dimensions, assets, backend and quality settings.
Measure actual frame times and native/WebContent resource behavior.
Separate warm-up from steady-state and repeat after a fresh launch.
Run a sustained session on a physical Duo when access exists.
Use results to ratify or revise provisional budgets before hero-asset volume expands.

acceptance.requirement: A physical Duo report records device/OS/build, sustained duration and frame-time percentiles under reproducible conditions.
Budget revisions cite measurements and preserve visual targets rather than claiming theoretical hardware capacity.

tests: Run the documented performance capture sequence with fixed scene and camera.
Record thermal state and limitations of any unavailable GPU timing counters.
risks: Simulator throughput must not be used as the phone baseline.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

phases.title: Swift native application shell
phases.goal: Turn the initial native harness into an accessible, recoverable application host.
phases.exit_gate: Native lifecycle, error handling, scene ownership and settings work before production content depends on them.

tasks.title: Establish application and scene ownership
steps: Define app launch, scene activation, loading, ready, failed and recovering states.
Keep one active authoritative layout session; reject accidental concurrent writers.
Model transient inner/outer display transitions separately from new documents.
Render native progress and recoverable error UI before web readiness.
Remove forced orientation and fixed-size assumptions.
Add structured local diagnostic events without transmitting analytics.

acceptance.requirement: Launch, scene recreation and inactive/active transitions produce one valid session and no duplicate engine host.
A failed renderer initialization shows actionable native UI instead of an indefinite blank view.

tests: Run lifecycle state-machine fixtures and launch UI tests.
Inject delayed readiness and initialization failure in the packaged app.
risks: Multiple native scenes can silently contend for the same save.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Implement lifecycle cancellation and WebContent recovery
steps: Cancel pending tasks when the host is replaced or the scene closes.
Remove message handlers and observers deterministically.
Handle WebContent process termination with a visible recovery state.
Retry only a bounded number of times with diagnostics.
Restore the most recent durable checkpoint once persistence is available.
Test rapid launch/background/foreground sequences and cancellation races.

acceptance.requirement: Repeated host creation/destruction does not retain handlers, duplicate messages or crash.
Injected content-process termination yields a bounded recovery or explicit error state, never an infinite restart loop.

tests: Run host lifetime and cancellation race tests.
Terminate WebContent in the simulator and inspect recovery logs.
risks: Recovered renderer readiness is not proof that unsaved layout edits were durable.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Build native preferences and accessible shell controls
steps: Define versioned preferences separately from layout documents.
Add sound, haptics, reduced-effects and interaction settings with explicit defaults.
Use native semantic controls, labels and Dynamic Type.
Make errors and support information reachable without the 3D canvas.
Respect system reduce-motion and mute behavior where applicable.
Test preference migration and invalid stored values.

acceptance.requirement: Preferences survive relaunch, reject invalid values and do not corrupt layout state.
Native settings can be navigated with VoiceOver and large text without clipped essential controls.

tests: Run preferences decode/migration fixtures.
Capture largest supported text layout and VoiceOver focus order.
risks: Custom decorative controls can conceal essential accessibility semantics.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Harden native app packaging and configuration
steps: Document bundle identifiers as project configuration, not secret values.
Inventory Info.plist keys and justify each entitlement or permission.
Exclude debug tools and test data from release resources.
Bundle versioned web assets with a build manifest and hashes.
Build a clean unsigned simulator app from generated project files.
Validate version/build metadata and diagnostic artifact collection.

acceptance.requirement: Fresh generation and build package the correct web manifest and no development server or secret material.
Every shipped permission/entitlement is justified and unnecessary capabilities are absent.

tests: Inspect compiled bundle resources and Info.plist.
Compare two clean builds' normalized resource manifests.
risks: Generated Xcode project drift can obscure the actual build inputs.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

phases.title: Secure native-to-web contract
phases.goal: Make native/WebView communication bounded, versioned, testable and resilient to stale sessions.
phases.exit_gate: Both implementations pass identical message fixtures and recover correctly from malformed, late and duplicate traffic.

tasks.title: Ratify the shared bridge schema
steps: Enumerate permitted directions and message types.
Define envelope version, message ID, session ID and payload size limits.
Specify finite numeric values, coordinate units and optional-field semantics.
Introduce error codes and request/response correlation without generic eval.
Generate identical valid and invalid fixture sets for both languages.
Version changes add migrations or explicit incompatible-version handling.

acceptance.requirement: Swift and TypeScript accept/reject the same shared fixtures, including unknown versions and non-finite inputs.
The schema limits message types, sizes and directions; no arbitrary script or filesystem method exists.

tests: Run cross-language fixture parity checks.
Verify older schema input fails visibly instead of being partially applied.
risks: Divergent validators create state disagreement at the platform boundary.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Implement handshake, ordering and session replacement
steps: Wait for web readiness before bootstrap and state restoration.
Tag traffic with the current session generation.
Drop late replies from a replaced WebView.
Bound outstanding requests and define timeout/cancel behavior.
Deduplicate durable commands using command IDs.
Test reordered, duplicated and delayed messages.

acceptance.requirement: Commands from stale sessions never mutate the active layout or preferences.
Timeouts and duplicate messages produce the documented outcomes without unbounded queues.

tests: Inject handshake delays, reply reorder and host replacement.
Assert the maximum pending-request count under sustained artificial traffic.
risks: Blind retries can apply an edit twice.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Deliver viewport and hinge data without coupling simulation
steps: Obtain content bounds and reserved regions from native geometry.
Serialize logical units and explicitly named angle units.
Coalesce high-frequency changes to the newest pending sample.
Apply geometry before hit-testing and drawing the next frame.
Keep hinge effect values out of track topology and clock state.
Exercise split-view, rotated and inner/outer transition fixtures.

acceptance.requirement: Viewport changes preserve correct picking coordinates and occlusion-safe controls across tested geometries.
Rapid hinge updates remain bounded and cannot advance, pause or reset simulation accidentally.

tests: Run geometry conversion round-trip fixtures.
Replay rapid posture/resize samples and verify queue bounds.
risks: Raw hinge angle is not an authoritative layout API.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Implement durable command and snapshot transfer
steps: Define snapshot revision and expected previous revision.
Transfer only validated serializable model data, never Three.js objects.
Bound snapshot size and reject unsupported document versions.
Return native persistence acknowledgments only after durable success.
Surface failures to the editor without discarding unsaved state.
Exercise interrupted transfer, retries and stale revisions.

acceptance.requirement: An acknowledgment identifies the committed document revision and is never emitted before successful storage.
Malformed, oversized and stale snapshots leave the previously committed document intact.

tests: Use an injected persistence stub to simulate disk full and interrupted writes.
Verify retries cannot overwrite a newer saved revision.
risks: Treating receipt as durability can lose user work.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Add bridge diagnostics and security regression coverage
steps: Record counts and error categories without storing sensitive layout contents.
Rate-limit repeated malformed input diagnostics.
Fuzz schema boundaries, long strings and deeply nested data.
Verify navigation cannot introduce another sender origin.
Exercise repeated pause/resume during active requests.
Document recovery steps and known platform limitations.

acceptance.requirement: Adversarial fixtures complete within bounded time/memory and preserve application state.
Diagnostics explain failures without leaking secrets or growing indefinitely.

tests: Run bounded fuzz fixtures under both decoders.
Review a deliberately corrupted bridge session from captured logs.
risks: Debug logging can become an accidental data store.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

phases.title: Deterministic simulation and physical scale
phases.goal: Establish a renderer-independent physical-miniature model kernel with reproducible time and geometry conventions.
phases.exit_gate: Fixed-step simulation, stable identity, model-meter units and replay invariants pass headless tests.

tasks.title: Ratify miniature units and coordinate conventions
steps: Use right-handed coordinates, Y up and XZ ground.
Adopt one world unit as one physical miniature meter.
Evaluate the proposed HO 1:87, 16.5 mm gauge and 0.8 by 0.5 m baseboard.
Define locomotive forward axis, wheel pivots and angle units.
Separate prototype-scale labels from simulation/render transforms.
Render and numerically check a ruler, gauge and known-radius fixture.

acceptance.requirement: All geometry fixtures agree on units, axes and gauge within specified numeric tolerances.
The scale ADR records actual chosen dimensions without presenting them as device measurements.

tests: Round-trip asset/model transforms and compare known distances.
Check gauge spacing and wheel circumference against the calibration fixture.
risks: Implicit prototype-to-model scaling causes train motion and asset-size mismatches.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Implement a fixed-step clock and deterministic random source
steps: Separate simulation ticks from renderer animation frames.
Choose and document the fixed tick interval and maximum catch-up work.
Define pause/resume and background elapsed-time policy.
Use seeded randomness only for reproducible simulation-affecting behavior.
Detect non-finite time inputs and timestamp reversals.
Compare identical command streams under different render frame schedules.

acceptance.requirement: Equivalent command streams produce matching model state at the same tick across 30, 60 and variable render schedules.
Long suspension cannot cause unbounded catch-up or a visible train teleport.

tests: Run clock tests including long gaps, negative deltas and repeated pause.
Hash replay snapshots at fixed intervals.
risks: A capped accumulator must have an explicit discarded-time policy.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Define entities, stable IDs and pure model boundaries
steps: Define track, turnout, train, consist and scenery entities.
Keep references by ID rather than mutable object pointer graphs.
Separate immutable asset definitions from editable instance state.
Validate referential integrity and bounds at model creation.
Exclude renderer handles, native objects and functions from serialization.
Test clone, serialize and deserialize behavior.

acceptance.requirement: The model can run and serialize in headless tests without WebGL, DOM or native APIs.
Duplicate IDs, missing references and invalid numeric state are rejected with actionable errors.

tests: Instantiate and advance a minimal model without renderer imports.
Round-trip a fixture and compare canonical state.
risks: Mesh names are not stable document IDs.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Implement command transactions and replay log
steps: Represent user actions as explicit typed commands.
Validate preconditions before mutating model state.
Apply a complete command atomically or reject it unchanged.
Assign monotonic sequence and transaction IDs.
Replay the same sequence from a known snapshot.
Define schema changes and invalid-command diagnostics.

acceptance.requirement: Invalid commands cannot partially mutate a layout, and valid replay reproduces the expected canonical state.
Command ordering and transaction boundaries remain stable across save/load cycles.

tests: Run replay fixtures with injected invalid and duplicate commands.
Compare before/after state digests when rejection is expected.
risks: Partial edit application makes later undo and persistence unreliable.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Install simulation invariants and debug observability
steps: Define bounds for speed, position, route indices and entity references.
Assert invariants after each transaction in debug builds.
Collect bounded per-tick diagnostics and replay seeds.
Keep production diagnostics lightweight and non-networked.
Run long headless sequences with repeatable generated commands.
Document how to minimize a failing replay.

acceptance.requirement: Long seeded runs preserve every declared invariant and produce reproducible failure traces when deliberately corrupted.
Debug checks do not leak into release behavior as unbounded logs or expensive per-object tracing.

tests: Run multiple fixed seeds and replay the recorded failing seed fixture.
Profile invariant overhead separately from production simulation.
risks: Determinism claims need reproducible seeds and canonical serialization.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Integrate the first operating-loop development workbench
deliverables: Playable fixed-loop native development slice with original procedural miniature art
Validated save/recovery, scenery editing and reproducible runtime evidence
steps: Integrate a deterministic analytic oval and a three-vehicle consist behind the existing native host.
Implement operating controls, camera views, lighting and bounded scenery transactions.
Implement strict native/browser document transport and atomic last-known-good persistence.
Exercise operate/edit/undo/save/reopen and malformed-input behavior in automated checks.
Capture actual web/native runtime evidence and record explicit remaining production gates.

acceptance.requirement: The packaged first-loop scene operates, edits, undoes and restores a durably acknowledged snapshot with automated web/native evidence.
Deterministic model, invalid commands, malformed/stale saves and recovery tests pass; prototype limits and remaining original roadmap gates are recorded.

tests: Run npm run check and the packaged browser suite.
Run the unchanged required native simulator workflow including storage/host tests.
Inspect actual runtime captures; identify procedural development art and hardware exclusions.
risks: This bounded oval must not be represented as a completed general track graph or production graphics.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

phases.title: Track geometry and connectivity
phases.goal: Create physically consistent modular track and authoritative route topology.
phases.exit_gate: Supported track pieces connect with continuous position/tangent and correct gauge; invalid layouts fail before operation.

tasks.title: Implement parametric track centerlines
steps: Represent supported pieces with explicit physical dimensions.
Evaluate position, tangent and curvature consistently.
Build monotonic arc-length lookup tables.
Handle endpoint and zero-length degeneracies.
Compare analytic straight/arc lengths with sampled values.

acceptance.requirement: Supported centerlines meet documented position, tangent and length tolerances.
Degenerate and out-of-range inputs fail without NaN transforms.

tests: Test straight, clockwise/counterclockwise arcs and endpoint samples.
Verify length accuracy at minimum supported radius.
risks: Uniform parameter sampling is not uniform speed.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Generate rails, sleepers and connector metadata
steps: Offset rail paths using a stable local frame.
Place sleepers by physical distance, not segment count.
Define connector position, direction, gauge and grade.
Keep rendering geometry separate from route topology.
Validate geometry through curves and module joints.

acceptance.requirement: Rail spacing and connector frames remain correct across supported pieces.
Reference captures show no gaps, reversed normals or intersecting rails at standard joints.

tests: Check connector transform round trips.
Capture close-ups of straight-to-curve and curve-to-curve joints.
risks: Render joins must not hide topological disconnections.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Build the route graph and connection validator
steps: Connect compatible sockets within explicit tolerances.
Preserve direction and route segment identity.
Detect disconnected ends and illegal overlapping connections.
Validate graph mutations atomically.
Traverse loops without infinite recursion.

acceptance.requirement: Valid circuits traverse indefinitely without losing route identity.
Mismatched gauge, endpoint tolerance and duplicate connections are rejected unchanged.

tests: Run loop, branch, disconnected and malformed graph fixtures.
Generate random valid edits and recheck referential integrity.
risks: A visually adjacent track is not necessarily connected.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Implement turnout routing and occupancy locks
steps: Model stock, straight and diverging routes explicitly.
Define switch states independently of decorative animation.
Track occupied route intervals for entire consists.
Reject or defer unsafe switching while occupied.
Preserve selected route through serialization and reversal.

acceptance.requirement: A train cannot teleport between turnout routes or switch beneath an occupying consist.
Invalid switching gives deterministic feedback and leaves topology unchanged.

tests: Traverse both routes in both directions.
Request switching while front, middle and rear vehicles occupy the turnout.
risks: Locomotive-only occupancy misses trailing carriages.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Validate grades, clearance and unsupported layouts
steps: Define initial supported grades and crossing rules.
Compute conservative swept clearance envelopes.
Detect intersections without valid bridge clearance.
Explain invalid placements with stable error categories.
Keep unsupported flexible track and complex crossings out of v1.

acceptance.requirement: Unsafe overlaps, excessive grades and unsupported joins are rejected before train placement.
Validation messages identify the conflicting pieces without forcing puzzle-style completion rules.

tests: Test minimum-radius, grade-boundary and bridge-clearance fixtures.
Check incomplete layouts remain editable even when not runnable.
risks: Editing freedom must coexist with safe operation constraints.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

phases.title: First operating railway
phases.goal: Operate a controllable miniature train on validated routes before final art expansion.
phases.exit_gate: A functional vertical slice runs forwards/reverse through loops and turnouts with stable rolling-stock placement.

tasks.title: Implement distance-based train motion
steps: Define bounded speed, acceleration and braking curves.
Integrate distance using the fixed simulation tick.
Cross route boundaries without position discontinuities.
Require a safe stop before direction reversal.
Handle track-end and removed-route conditions explicitly.

acceptance.requirement: Motion remains continuous through joins and independent of render FPS.
Stop, reverse and track-end behavior are deterministic and cannot leave invalid route indices.

tests: Replay identical throttle commands under varied render schedules.
Run a long-duration loop with periodic reversals.
risks: Route transitions must preserve excess traveled distance.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Place bogies, wheels and a small consist
steps: Resolve front/rear bogies by arc distance.
Maintain route history across turnouts and reversal.
Place carriage bodies from bogie frames.
Drive wheel rotation from actual traveled distance.
Clamp or reject unsupported consist/radius combinations.

acceptance.requirement: Bogie/wheel positions follow rails through supported curves and switches without visible floating.
Trailing vehicles preserve the selected route after the locomotive leaves a turnout.

tests: Capture minimum-radius curves, turnout passage and reversal.
Compare wheel phase with distance divided by circumference.
risks: Rigid body rotation at a single point can derail visual bogies.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Add operating controls and railroad interactions
steps: Map controls to validated model commands.
Provide large emergency-stop and speed feedback.
Make turnout selection visible without relying on color.
Separate control gestures from camera gestures.
Add stationary and moving control-state tests.

acceptance.requirement: Every operating control changes the intended model command and provides understandable feedback.
Stop remains reachable during camera movement, resizing and error recovery.

tests: Run native/WebView interaction smoke tests.
Exercise control commands during viewport transitions.
risks: Decorative controls must not become inaccessible canvas-only targets.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Approve the functional vertical slice
steps: Assemble an original oval, turnout and short siding.
Run throttle, braking, reverse and safe switching.
Exercise pause/resume and host recovery.
Capture a continuous interaction video and diagnostic trace.
Record unresolved visual work as unfinished, not accepted photorealism.

acceptance.requirement: The representative layout operates through the documented command sequence without simulation or bridge errors.
The evidence identifies placeholder art and does not conflate functional success with final appearance.

tests: Repeat the full slice sequence after clean app launch.
Compare final model state with the expected replay snapshot.
risks: A flattering static shot does not prove an operating railway.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

phases.title: Document persistence and recovery
phases.goal: Protect user-created layouts with explicit schema, transactions and durable native storage.
phases.exit_gate: Layouts survive relaunch, corruption, interruption and migration without silent loss.

tasks.title: Define the versioned layout document format
steps: Separate layout design from transient render state.
Define schema version, IDs, metadata and asset references.
Validate document size, counts and numeric bounds.
Specify unknown-field and missing-asset behavior.
Create canonical serialization and compatibility fixtures.

acceptance.requirement: Both native and web validators agree on document validity and supported versions.
Serialization excludes renderer/native handles and reproduces stable model identity.

tests: Round-trip minimal, maximum-budget and malformed layouts.
Reject future-version documents with a recoverable explanation.
risks: Saving all runtime state can freeze accidental implementation details.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Implement atomic native save and last-known-good recovery
steps: Write validated data to a temporary sibling file.
Flush and replace using documented native file operations.
Retain a bounded last-known-good version.
Acknowledge only successful durable revision changes.
Recover from corrupt primary data without overwriting evidence.

acceptance.requirement: Interrupted writes never replace a valid document with partial data.
Corrupt-primary recovery preserves the backup and informs the user what was restored.

tests: Inject failures before write, replacement and acknowledgment.
Simulate disk-full, missing directory and corrupted checksum cases.
risks: Error handling must not delete the only remaining good save.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Implement schema migrations and asset-ID compatibility
steps: Create immutable historical fixture documents.
Migrate stepwise with validation between versions.
Preserve an original backup before migration.
Map renamed asset IDs explicitly rather than by display name.
Reject irreversible migrations unless an export path exists.

acceptance.requirement: Every supported historical fixture migrates without lost track topology or scenery identity.
Migration failure leaves the original document and last-known-good copy recoverable.

tests: Run migration fixtures repeatedly to confirm idempotent loading.
Test missing/deprecated asset definitions.
risks: Changing asset filenames is not a valid migration strategy.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Implement undo, redo and autosave transaction boundaries
steps: Store reversible commands or bounded before/after patches.
Coalesce continuous drags into one user transaction.
Clear redo history after a new divergent edit.
Autosave only consistent committed model revisions.
Retain visible unsaved status until native acknowledgment.

acceptance.requirement: Undo/redo restores exact topology and scenery state across mixed edit sequences.
Autosave cannot persist an intermediate invalid drag state or mark failed writes as saved.

tests: Replay alternating track/scenery edits with undo and redo.

Draft accurate title, subtitle and description without ranking/revenue claims.
Obtain explicit owner approval for price, currencies, territories and metadata.

acceptance.requirement: The owner approves the exact price/currency/territory configuration and documented device eligibility.
Metadata advertises only implemented supported functionality and contains no false exclusivity claim.

tests: Inspect storefront eligibility and price configuration through authorized access.
Cross-check every feature claim against the release feature matrix.
risks: An in-app rejection screen does not prevent unsupported customers from purchasing.

tasks.title: Prepare genuine screenshots, previews and reviewer notes
steps: Capture store screenshots from the release-intended app.
Use current Apple asset specifications without invented dimensions.
Disclose the offline toy, folding behavior and any review setup needs.
Provide reviewer access instructions without secret leakage.
Verify screenshots and videos contain only shipping content.

acceptance.requirement: Store assets are traceable to actual running app content and satisfy current official format requirements.
Reviewer notes accurately explain tested device requirements and feature behavior.

tests: Validate asset dimensions/encoding against current Apple documentation.
Have an unfamiliar reviewer follow the instructions from a clean install.
risks: Concept renders must not be presented as in-app screenshots.

phases.title: Release candidate and final authorization
phases.goal: Produce one immutable candidate with complete engineering, device, art and owner evidence.
phases.exit_gate: A frozen candidate passes all mandatory gates and receives explicit owner permission to submit.

tasks.title: Freeze scope and audit dependency/evidence completeness
steps: Select the candidate source commit and exact dependency set.
Check every required predecessor and manual gate.
Identify stale evidence when relevant source/assets changed.
Record all residual issues with severity and approved workaround.
Freeze scope; route new ideas to post-launch backlog.

acceptance.requirement: Every release gate has valid build-relevant evidence or an explicitly approved nonblocking limitation.
No unknown, failed or skipped required check is represented as passed.

tests: Run the project validator and audit acceptance evidence manually.
Compare evidence source digests with candidate inputs.
risks: A long checklist is not complete when its evidence applies to an older build.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Build and verify the candidate from a clean environment
steps: Generate the project and bundle from a clean checkout.
Verify all hashes and version identifiers.
Build, sign and install the exact candidate.
Run automated and critical physical-device regression checks.
Archive logs/results without silently rebuilding a different candidate.

acceptance.requirement: The candidate archive is reproducible from the recorded source and toolchain inputs.
The exact candidate passes critical physical-device workflows and supported posture tests.

tests: Run the final operating/edit/save/fold/backup sequence.
Compare signed archive resource hashes with the approved manifest.
risks: Rebuilding after testing can invalidate candidate provenance.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Rehearse backup, hotfix and release rollback limits
steps: Rehearse restoration from exported user-layout fixtures.
Confirm previous document versions remain loadable.
Document what store release controls can and cannot undo.
Prepare a main-branch hotfix path with preserved evidence.
Identify owner contacts and stop-release triggers.

acceptance.requirement: The team can recover representative documents and prepare a data-safe hotfix without destructive Git operations.
The runbook accurately distinguishes stopping rollout from downgrading installed user applications.

tests: Execute a mock critical-regression scenario without publishing anything.
Verify the recovery process preserves current user documents.
risks: App-store rollback does not automatically reverse installed data migrations.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Obtain final owner submission authorization
steps: Present exact candidate build, source commit and gate summary.
Disclose residual risks and known limitations.
Confirm price, territories, eligibility and store assets.
Ask for authorization to submit, distinct from authorization to publish.
Record the owner's explicit decision and permitted actions.

acceptance.requirement: The owner explicitly authorizes submission of the identified candidate and configuration.
The authorization record states whether public release is also approved or remains a separate gate.

tests: Verify approval refers to the unchanged candidate.
Stop if material code, asset or storefront configuration changes afterward.
risks: Finishing development does not authorize store submission automatically.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

phases.title: Authorized submission and launch
phases.goal: Submit and release only the approved candidate, then monitor the actual outcome.
phases.exit_gate: Publication state, review decisions and early defects are recorded honestly with owner-controlled release actions.

tasks.title: Submit the approved candidate for review
steps: Verify authorization and exact build before submission.
Check reviewer notes, eligibility and metadata one final time.
Submit through the approved account workflow.
Record actual processing/review status without predicting approval.
Leave a handoff stating what external decision is pending.

acceptance.requirement: The submitted build and storefront configuration exactly match owner authorization.
The repository records actual submission identifiers and status, not an assumed approval.

tests: Compare submitted build number/source manifest with the candidate.
Verify no accidental automatic-release setting changed the authorization scope.
risks: Submission success is not review acceptance.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Handle review feedback without bypassing safeguards
steps: Read the actual reviewer message and classify the issue.
Explain existing behavior with evidence where appropriate.
Implement only authorized scope-compatible fixes.
Re-run affected gates and obtain renewed approval if the candidate changes.
Record approval, rejection or pending status faithfully.

acceptance.requirement: Every review response and candidate change is traceable to actual feedback and required retests.
No private API, deceptive capability or misleading metadata is added to evade review.

tests: Review the submitted response against actual runtime behavior.
Repeat changed eligibility, privacy or workflow checks.
risks: Review pressure must not override the user-data and distribution rules.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Release publicly after explicit owner approval
steps: Confirm store review approval and candidate identity.
Obtain any still-required public-release authorization.
Apply only the approved release/territory timing.
Verify the actual public listing and supported purchase eligibility.
Record the release version and observed availability.

acceptance.requirement: The owner explicitly authorizes the public release action taken.
Actual public availability and metadata are verified after release rather than inferred from a button click.

tests: Inspect the published listing in intended territories.
Confirm version, price and eligibility against approval.
risks: Approval to submit is not necessarily approval to publish.

tasks.title: Complete early-launch monitoring and triage
steps: Review authorized crash reports and support channels.
Separate observed sales/reviews from estimates.
Prioritize data loss, crashes and purchase-eligibility defects.
Use the incident runbook for owner-approved corrective action.
Record a concrete handoff into maintenance.

acceptance.requirement: Observed launch issues are triaged with severity, reproduction details and responsible next actions.
Revenue, adoption and reliability summaries clearly distinguish actual data from unavailable information.

tests: Verify every critical issue has a stop/release/hotfix decision owner.
Check that support answers do not promise unplanned features.
risks: Absence of reports is not proof that no users encountered defects.

phases.title: Maintenance and next-version discipline
phases.goal: Keep the released miniature railway reliable without losing saves, quality or the owner's original scope.
phases.exit_gate: The first maintenance cycle is documented; future work receives new stable tasks rather than rewriting completed history.

tasks.title: Establish recurring defect and support triage
steps: Define who reviews authorized crash/support information.
Assign severity and reproduction requirements.
Preserve user privacy in attached diagnostic data.
Convert confirmed defects into stable new backlog tasks.
Document cadence without claiming an unscheduled monitor is running.

acceptance.requirement: A concrete owner-approved maintenance process identifies inputs, cadence and escalation rules.
Confirmed issues have actionable tasks rather than unsupported completion claims.

tests: Triage a real or clearly labelled rehearsal issue end to end.
Verify no automation is represented as active unless actually configured.
risks: A written monitoring plan is not an operating monitoring service.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Review OS, SDK and dependency compatibility updates
steps: Recheck official platform and dependency release notes.
Run existing fixtures before changing version pins.
Evaluate native origin, hinge, renderer and asset decoder regressions.
Upgrade in a bounded main-branch checkpoint with rollback-safe data behavior.
Record actual compatibility results and unresolved blockers.

acceptance.requirement: The first compatibility review records tested versions and observed results.
No dependency/SDK update bypasses save, device or visual regression gates.

tests: Run packaged asset-origin and posture smoke tests on the proposed toolchain.
Compare key reference captures before accepting renderer upgrades.
risks: A minor renderer upgrade can alter color, shaders or asset extension behavior.
tasks.estimated_sessions: 1–3 focused sessions; planning estimate, not a delivery promise

tasks.title: Ship a data-safe maintenance update when authorized
deliverables: Authorized maintenance candidate or documented no-update decision
steps: Choose a bounded defect set from observed issues.
Preserve historical document fixtures and migration paths.
Re-run affected engineering/device/art gates.
Obtain approval for any upload, submission or public update.
Record the actual update outcome or justified no-release decision.

acceptance.requirement: Any shipped maintenance build preserves supported user documents and passes relevant regression gates; a no-update outcome is explicitly owner-approved.
The owner approves release actions or explicitly records that no update is needed.

tests: Load/export older real-world fixture layouts on the maintenance candidate.
Repeat the release authorization and provenance checks.
risks: A hotfix must not silently reset incompatible saves.

tasks.title: Create the next-version backlog without erasing history
steps: Review actual demand and maintenance findings before expanding content.
Keep original no-puzzle/offline/Duo scope unless the owner changes it.
Assign new stable task IDs for new features or releases.
Preserve completed evidence and supersede decisions explicitly.
Leave a next-version handoff with ready work and owner gates.

acceptance.requirement: Future work has explicit dependencies and acceptance criteria without renumbering or erasing completed tasks.
Scope changes require recorded owner approval rather than speculative feature creep.

tests: Run task-graph validation after backlog extension.
Verify a fresh agent can identify the next ready task from repository state.
risks: Maintenance is ongoing; completing this setup cycle does not mean all future work is finished.
